task.description: TEST-DESIGNER pass (WF-02 Step 3) on REQ-167. ELIXIR-DEV already wrote an initial test suite (test/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate_test.exs, 16 tests, all passing per step-02a/step-02c/step-02d's independent reruns). Your job is a MUTATION-DRIVEN review and strengthening pass, not a rewrite: read the shipped capability_gate.ex (commit 69e8722) and the existing test file in full, then find and fill real coverage gaps by actually mutating the implementation locally and confirming the existing suite fails to catch each mutation before adding a test that does. Use export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" and WASMEX_BUILD=true for wasmex-touching mix commands. Revert every mutation before finishing -- mutate locally, verify, git checkout -- to restore, never leave the implementation altered.
acceptance_criteria: Mutate build_import_table/1 to use an allow-everything-then-filter-out approach instead of filter-then-group (or simpler: change the MapSet.member?/2 check to always return true) and confirm an existing test catches a manifest with zero capabilities still producing a non-empty table; if not, add a test.

Mutate start_instance/2 to supply a hardcoded :wasi key (simulating an accidental future regression that grants filesystem access) and confirm an existing test catches this -- if wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open is still rejected only because the registry lacks it (not because :wasi is absent), a mutation that adds :wasi with default (permissive) WASI options might let path_open resolve; verify what actually happens and strengthen the AC3 test if the current one wouldn't catch a real :wasi-key regression.

Mutate the crash-classification regex/pattern match (classify_crash/1's unresolved-import branch) to always fall through to the generic {:crashed, raw_reason} branch and confirm an existing test distinguishes {:unresolved_import, ns, fn} from a generic {:crashed, _} result (i.e. asserts the SPECIFIC tuple shape, not just that {:error, _} was returned).

Mutate start_instance/2's success branch to call GenServer.stop/1 on the pid before returning it (accidentally adopting ModuleRegistry's pattern) and confirm an existing test catches that the returned pid is still alive/usable after start_instance/2 returns {:ok, pid} -- add a test if none exists asserting Process.alive?(pid) immediately after a successful call.

Confirm the crash-propagation-containment test (start_instance/2 on an unresolved-import module must not crash the calling test process) verifies the test process is NOT trap_exit at the point of the call, matching REQ-166's own equivalent mutation-tested assertion (module_registry_test.exs).

Confirm build_import_table/1 with an empty manifest.capabilities list produces exactly %{} (not a partially-empty nested map like %{"env" => %{}}) -- add a test if this exact shape isn't already asserted.
Do not modify lib/letflow/engine/wasm/capability_gate.ex, lib/letflow/application.ex, module_registry.ex, or plugin_handler.ex -- test/fixture files only.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary: Mutation-driven strengthening pass on capability_gate_test.exs (16 -> 18 tests). Six mutations applied locally against 69e8722's capability_gate.ex, each verified caught/not-caught before/after, each reverted (git diff/status confirm implementation byte-identical to 69e8722). Four of six mutations were already caught by the existing 16 tests; two were not and got new tests: (1) empty-manifest exact-shape gap (build_import_table(%{capabilities: []}) accepted a namespace-present-but-empty %{"env" => %{}} under the old assertions -- new test asserts == %{} exactly), (2) success-branch pid-liveness gap (GenServer.stop/1 accidentally called before returning {:ok, pid} only surfaced as an incidental double-stop crash in existing tests, never as a direct assertion -- new test asserts Process.alive?(pid) immediately after a successful call). Full findings with actual mix test output for every mutation are in test/specs/REQ-167.md's new addendum section. No implementation defect found; no candidate issue filed.

mutation_findings.evidence: Enum.filter replaced with fn _ -> true end; mix test result: 11/16 passed, Failed: 5 tests, including the empty-capabilities test at capability_gate_test.exs:92

Wasmex.start_link/1 called with wasi: true added; mix test result: 14/16 passed, Failed: 2 tests -- both AC3/path_open tests, which returned {:ok, pid} instead of {:error, {:instantiation_denied, {:unresolved_import, ...}}} because wasi: true natively resolves wasi_snapshot_preview1/path_open

Regex.named_captures call's case subject replaced with a hardcoded nil; mix test result: 11/16 passed, Failed: 5 tests -- AC1/AC3 tests fail because they assert the specific {:unresolved_import, ns, fn} tuple, not just {:error, _}

mutation_findings.criterion: AC4 (start_instance success branch calls GenServer.stop/1 before returning)
mutation_findings.evidence: Before new test: mix test result 13/16 passed, Failed: 3 tests, but only via an incidental double-GenServer.stop crash in unrelated tests, never a direct liveness assertion. Added 'the returned pid is alive and usable immediately after a successful call' (assert Process.alive?(pid)). After: mutation re-applied, mix test result 14/18 passed, Failed: 4 tests, cleanly including the new test.

Already present at capability_gate_test.exs:48, assert Process.info(test_pid, :trap_exit) == {:trap_exit, false}, matching module_registry_test.exs's equivalent assertion. Confirmed present; no new test needed.
